name: Daria Nakamura

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you would say at work and what you think privately. What does a normal day involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m Daria, 43, and I lead the developers maintaining emergency-call routing software at a tech company. I have a master’s degree and I’m the person they ask when a call takes a strange path. I read overnight routing reports, trace failures and sign off on fixes before the next release. I have never used an AI tool; I need to know why a call went to one desk rather than another.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is riding on your salary at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Leon, cooks in a school kitchen, and we have two children in school and a mortgage. My pay is low for a lead developer, and we have less than one month of expenses saved. There are few similar jobs nearby. A recent roof repair took what little cushion we had.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AI Plateau leaves emergency routing in experienced hands. A routine sorter might save minutes, but a person must check every change that sends a call to a desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I would be glad my skill still matters. I would not feel financially safe, because one missed pay period after that roof bill would put the mortgage at risk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep signing off routing fixes and tracing failed calls myself. I’d put 35 into a mortgage buffer after payday only if Leon gets his normal kitchen hours. In the first year I’d ask my manager to revisit my lead salary with evidence from the last safe release.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about money, though not about AI in this picture. The roof is fixed, but the savings account is almost empty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you bring to a pay conversation?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show my manager the routing failure we caught before a call reached the wrong desk. I would ask for a review date, not spend a raise we have not received.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Leon about spending?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Leon we can keep the children’s school trips but delay replacing the living-room sofa. If his kitchen hours fall, that plan changes.

say: I expect **AI Plateau** to leave emergency routing with experienced reviewers.
I would require **human sign-off** on every call-routing change.
think: I feel **relieved** my specialist skill remains valuable.
I fear the **mortgage** after a roof repair emptied our savings.
do: **Keep** tracing failed calls and signing off routing fixes.
**Save** 35 after payday only when Leon’s kitchen hours hold.
**Request** a lead-pay review with safe-release evidence; delay replacing our sofa while protecting school trips.
feel: **Anxious** about existing bills despite steady routing work.
S0.quote: The roof is fixed, but the savings account is almost empty.
fieldNote: Her **strong technical standing** does not offset low pay and an emptied cushion.
The **35 transfer** depends on kitchen hours; a salary increase is only a request.

steps.text: Keep tracing failed emergency calls and signing off routing fixes
Save 35 after payday only when kitchen hours hold
Delay living-room sofa replacement while keeping children’s school trips

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will let AI draft code, check routes and answer callers faster. I would ask management to prove the new checker works before reducing our review team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think a lead title could still be cut if software handles routine tracing. I have never used AI. A manager might confuse caution about emergency calls with refusal to work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask our call supervisor to run the approved checker against twenty past misrouted calls while I verify each destination. If it catches all twenty, I’d learn its review screen during paid time. In the first year, if our team is cut, I’d search for actual network-support openings before resigning and ask the employer for written notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. I expect the team could shrink and my pay might be the part removed, with almost no savings to bridge it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which old call would judge the checker?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show the call supervisor the night a transfer loop sent a caller back to the same desk. The checker must catch that loop before I sign a release.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children about cuts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children that my hours have not changed yet. If they do, Leon and I would cancel the planned sports camp, not their school meals.

say: I expect **Steady Disruption** to speed code, route checks and caller answers.
I would require **proof on old calls** before cutting reviewers.
think: I fear my **lead title** will not prevent a team cut.
I worry my **AI caution** could be mistaken for unwillingness to work.
do: **Test** an approved checker on twenty old misrouted calls with the supervisor.
**Learn** its review screen during paid time only if all twenty pass.
**Search** real network jobs if cut; cancel sports camp if hours fall, protecting school meals.
feel: **Anxious** about a possible pay loss with almost no cushion.
S1.quote: A manager might confuse caution about emergency calls with refusal to work.
fieldNote: Her **AI trial** has a twenty-call gate and paid learning time, grounded in real routing harm.
She expects **personal income risk** from a smaller team despite senior skill and a lead title.

steps.text: Learn approved routing checker during paid time if twenty old calls pass
Search actual network-support jobs if the review team is cut
Cancel planned sports camp only if developer hours fall; protect school meals

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 reaches emergency-routing code in 2028. Hands-on robots arrive around 2031, so Leon’s kitchen work may have more time than my desk job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect my team could be reduced to almost nothing. We do not have enough cash for one full mortgage payment if my salary ends.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my employer for written severance and call the mortgage lender before a missed payment to learn the hardship terms. I’d stop the planned sofa purchase and keep the cash for food and transport. In the first year after 2028, if laid off, I’d apply for real local openings and eligible income help.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed and awake at night. Two years until AGI by 2028 gives me time for calls, but not enough time to rebuild our roof-drained savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you need from the lender?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the lender which documents are needed and get the answer in writing. I would not assume the mortgage can pause because I am worried.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to Leon that night?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Leon exactly which bills the next pay covers. I would not ask him to take extra kitchen shifts that do not exist.

say: I expect **AGI by 2028** to reach routing code before hands-on robots arrive.
I would tell colleagues Leon’s **kitchen work** may change later.
think: I expect the **routing team** could nearly disappear.
Our **empty savings** cannot carry a mortgage payment after lost developer pay.
do: **Request** written severance and lender hardship requirements before arrears.
**Cancel** the sofa purchase while protecting food and work transport.
**Apply** for real jobs and eligible income help if dismissed after 2028.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected pay loss and roof-drained savings.
S2.quote: Two years until AGI by 2028 gives me time for calls, but not enough time to rebuild our roof-drained savings.
fieldNote: Her **code shock** is in 2028, with hands-on robots around 2031 for kitchen work.
The **lender inquiry** is not guaranteed relief; public help depends on eligibility and jobs on openings.

steps.text: Cancel planned sofa and keep cash for food and transport
Apply for actual local jobs if dismissed after 2028
Apply for eligible income help if dismissed after 2028
Call mortgage lender about hardship documents before missing a payment

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives five years to document what happens when an emergency call takes a wrong turn. Thinking AI reaches my code in 2031; hands-on robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I still think the coding team could shrink, but I can learn more of the call centre’s procedures while earning. I cannot assume that procedure work stays paid after full thinking AI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask for one paid afternoon monthly with the call supervisor to learn how transfer failures are investigated. I’d use the free emergency-communications guide if paid time is refused. In the first year after 2031, if my role ends, I’d apply only for real service-quality openings that pay enough for our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about future work, with more time to test another skill. Our mortgage bill still arrives every month before AGI by 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you prove you learned service quality?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would write up one transfer loop and ask the supervisor to mark where my explanation misses the caller’s experience. That is better evidence than a certificate I cannot afford.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for training?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not buy a course with our thin reserve. If the company approves the afternoon, I can learn while still paid; otherwise I will read the free guide.

say: I see **AGI by 2031** as time to document misrouted calls.
I know **2034 robots** follow the earlier code change.
think: I expect a **smaller coding team** despite warning.
I cannot assume **call procedures** stay paid after full thinking AI.
do: **Learn** transfer-failure review monthly on paid approved time with a supervisor-marked case.
**Use** the free communications guide if paid time is refused.
**Apply** for actual mortgage-paying service-quality jobs if coding ends after 2031.
feel: **Anxious** about future income and current mortgage bills.
S3.quote: Our mortgage bill still arrives every month before AGI by 2031.
fieldNote: She tests **service-quality skill** with a marked case, without assuming AGI leaves the role intact.
Her **paid afternoon** needs approval; free guidance is the fallback and any role needs adequate pay.

steps.text: Learn monthly transfer review with paid approval and marked case; otherwise use free guide
Apply after 2031 only to mortgage-paying service-quality jobs if coding ends

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2036 gives a decade to improve emergency routing and train successors. Thinking AI reaches code in 2036; hands-on robots come around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect my work to hold for now, but the low pay and empty reserve still keep me awake. Ten years before AGI does not pay this month’s mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep signing off routing changes and show a junior developer one failed-call trace each month. I’d save 35 after payday only when Leon’s hours hold and ask for a written pay-review date this year. In the first year after 2036, if code work ends, I’d search actual openings before considering a move with the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about current money, though I have time to plan work changes. I would rather teach a real trace than buy a course brochure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the junior developer practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the junior developer to explain a transfer loop back to me before touching a release. If they cannot, we try again together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the children for work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Leon and I would keep the children in their current school unless an actual offer covers a new mortgage and travel. We would not move them for an advert.

say: I see **AGI by 2036** as time to improve routing and train successors.
I know **2039 robots** follow the earlier code change.
think: I expect my **job** to hold in the near term.
I still face **low pay** and thin savings despite a decade to prepare.
do: **Keep** signing off routing fixes and teaching one failed-call trace monthly.
**Save** 35 after payday only when Leon’s kitchen hours hold; request a written pay-review date this year.
**Search** actual openings after 2036 if coding work ends.
feel: **Anxious** about present bills, with time for later work planning.
S4.quote: Ten years before AGI does not pay this month’s mortgage.
fieldNote: Her **baseline money strain** stays despite long warning and strong technical standing.
She asks for a **pay-review date** now and would move only for a real offer covering family costs.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my routing pay could end before we rebuild any mortgage cushion. Written severance, a clear lender process and paid time to learn service quality would help. I would also need actual openings, not a promise that someone will always answer emergency calls.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask where a caller goes when the routing screen says every desk is free but none answers. An unanswered emergency call still belongs to a person waiting on the line.

headlineQuote: An unanswered emergency call still belongs to a person waiting on the line.
portrait: Daria is a **43-year-old lead developer** with a master’s degree and strong skill in emergency-call routing code.
Her **low lead pay**, mortgage, two children and roof-drained savings below one month create baseline anxiety.
She has **never used AI** and requires twenty real routing cases before trying an approved checker.
She seeks **written terms**, paid procedural learning and actual vacancies while keeping lender inquiries separate from public aid.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her routing salary before the household rebuilds a mortgage cushion.
whatWouldHelp: **Written severance**, clear lender terms and paid service-quality learning would help.
